as Miyamoto user # Credentials found via curl # ```bashUser: miyamotoPassword: Pa847word987@Joomla456```Once we’re inside the dashboard we take advantage of the currently running template by going into System->Templates->Administrator Templates. Once there, we can inject our php shell code into the index.php file (the main page) and save our changes. Then we have our listener running and refresh the main page on the web server and get a reverse shell back as www-data.
After looking around for a bit, we find our user flag which is in an unconventional place (not in the home folder). Then we proceed to escalate our privileges by running sudo -l this will help us see if we can run anything as sudo without a password.
Shell as root user # Once you find the file we can run as root without a password we can run the following command to get into the root shell
```bash {hl_lines=[1]}www-data@streetcoder:/opt/backup$ sudo ./DbMaria 'test; /bin/bash -p #'/*M!999999\- enable the sandbox mode */ -- MariaDB dump 10.19 Distrib 10.6.23-MariaDB, for debian-linux-gnu (x86_64)---- Host: localhost Database: test-- -------------------------------------------------------- Server version 10.6.23-MariaDB-0ubuntu0.22.04.1```This will let us get the root flag located in ~/root/root.txt and with that, we have compromised the machine.
